title: Kharge-Rijiju face-off in Rajya Sabha; opposition stalls House over Amit Shah
description: The Rajya Sabha approved the Appropriation Bill, 2026, authorizing fund withdrawals for excess expenditure. Opposition members repeatedly demanded Home Minister Amit Shah's presence in the House.  Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju was asked to convey their sentiments to Shah.  Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge sought the Home Minister's statement on student police action.  The opposition also requested the Prime Minister's apology for the alleged police excesses.

title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
description: In a significant move, the Supreme Court has granted interim bail for one week to Sumit Roy, who serves as the personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. Roy is implicated in the Salboni land-grabbing case, which followed the arrest of former TMC MLA Sujoy Hazra. Notably, the court has stayed Roy's arrest until it reconvenes for the next hearing.

title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
description: The Lok Sabha has taken a vital step by passing a bill aimed at simplifying tax rules to enhance investment attractiveness. The new legislation abolishes a limitation on specific electronic payment options, allowing banks and providers to charge merchants on transactions. Additionally, the government is empowered to revise the zero-MDR scheme for UPI and RuPay. This initiative is poised to drive advancements in the financial sector’s infrastructure and innovative capabilities.

title: Amid cyber threats, IT ministry asked to expedite hirings
description: The finance ministry has sanctioned more posts for CERT-In, yet the hiring remains underway. With rising cyber threats dominating discussions, a parliamentary committee is pressing for expedited recruitment. The IndiaAI Mission's fellowship program initially struggled to attract candidates. In response, MeitY is implementing outreach sessions and promotional campaigns to encourage more applicants. Additionally, final touches are being made to recruitment guidelines for several scientific roles ahead of future job advertisements.

title: China-Japan tensions escalate after Tokyo labels Beijing as its 'greatest strategic challenge'
description: The white paper approved by Japan's cabinet on Tuesday (August 4) said China's growing military actions are Japan’s top security challenge and “must be addressed through overall national strength and cooperation with allies and like-minded nations”

title: 15 Indian seafarers killed in West Asia and Black Sea conflicts: Regulator
description: Geopolitical conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea have endangered Indian seafarers.  Fifteen Indian seafarers have died and two remain missing in recent months.  Drone and missile attacks have become rampant in the Black Sea region.  Piracy off Somalia and Houthi threats have also resurfaced significantly.  India's maritime regulator is enhancing safety measures and tracking seafarers' well-being.

title: Sonam Wangchuk says Rahul Gandhi ignored his offer to end his fast
description: Sonam Wangchuk voiced disappointment with political leaders after his hunger strike concluded. His wife Gitanjali sought Rahul Gandhi's involvement but received no positive response. Union ministers also reportedly broke a promise regarding the release of photos. Wangchuk felt leaders showed a narrow approach and arrived late to his protest. He praised the apolitical CJP organization for its fair and just advocacy.

title: FCRA Bill is ‘religion-neutral’, Shah assures Christian bodies
description: Delegation meets Amit Shah; member says Home Minister has told them that the government has “no intention to harass the Christian community”; forum flags ‘deemed cessation of assets’ clause; Bill could be taken up for discussion in Parliament on August 12

title: Priyanka Chopra joins Russell Crowe in Hollywood sci-fi action thriller 'Bluefly'
description: Priyanka Chopra Jonas has announced her next Hollywood venture, a sci-fi action thriller.  She will star opposite Russell Crowe in the film titled 'Bluefly'.  The movie's plot involves a deep Congo mission to recover a mysterious downed aircraft.  This project marks another significant international role for the acclaimed Indian actress.  'Bluefly' is scheduled for production and release in the future.

title: CBI arrests four accused persons in tech-support fraud case
description: The CBI raided 10 locations across Punjab and Delhi, including a call centre operated from the premises of the main accused in Mohali in the intervening night of August 5 and 6

title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister over breakfast
description: A trio of dissenting Trinamool MPs is set to engage with Prime Minister Narendra Modi following their earlier discussions with Union Minister Amit Shah related to pressing concerns. Notably, these lawmakers have distanced themselves from two NDA meetings. Additionally, other NCPI representatives and Shiv Sena MPs are expected to join them for a breakfast meeting with the Prime Minister on Friday morning.

Supreme Court happy with progress in talks in Sunjay Kapur case
description: In an effort to resolve a high-profile family dispute, members are actively engaging in mediation under the supervision of ex-CJI DY Chandrachud, following a Supreme Court directive. So far, six sessions have taken place, where the parties have agreed to continue discussions. They are pursuing a comprehensive settlement related to trust claims, with mediation scheduled to run until November 2.

title: 5.7 lakh people fined Rs 5.1 cr in 2025-26 for smoking in public
description: In India, over 570,000 individuals were fined for smoking in public spaces, accumulating penalties exceeding Rs 51 million under the COTPA legislation. Karnataka led the charge, issuing the most fines. Interestingly, several states recorded no violations or fines throughout the year. Enforcement primarily lies with state governments, highlighting the varying levels of adherence to the public smoking ban.

title: 'It will end pretty soon': Trump hints at sooner resolution to US-Iran war
description: Expressing confidence, US President Trump suggested that the Iran conflict is nearing its end, arguing that Tehran cannot bear its continuation. He remains hopeful about negotiations related to the Strait of Hormuz. The US is resolute in preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. Meanwhile, Iran's defence minister asserts that their military is on standby for any potential threats, and the parliament speaker claims that the US.

title: SC says compulsory retirement not punitive, upholds CISF officer’s removal
description: The Supreme Court clarified that compulsory retirement is not a punishment for diminished performance, but rather a necessary step to uphold the standards of efficiency and discipline required. The court dismissed a plea from a CISF officer who disputed his removal after his performance had notably dropped from 'Good' to 'Average'. It emphasized the importance of consistent high performance among personnel in disciplined forces.

title: Can't exclude SC/ST creamy layer from quotas: Government to Supreme Court
description: The government is against extending the creamy layer to SC and ST reservation benefits, emphasizing that the challenges these communities face are rooted in more than economic issues. Reservation serves to right historical wrongs and ensure equitable access. The Supreme Court has permitted states to categorize castes within SC groups, but only Parliament holds the power to amend the lists of SC and ST populations eligible for these allocations.

title: Trump signs 2 immigration actions to limit birthright citizenship and curb 'birth tourism'
description: Trump said one will limit the number of people eligible for U.S. citizenship after being born in the United States

title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation
description: In a significant phone discussion, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu evaluated the progress made in their strategic partnership and bilateral engagements. They also addressed current developments in West Asia, amidst Israel's increasing international scrutiny due to its military actions. This exchange highlights their continued efforts to bolster cooperation and deepen ties between India and Israel.

title: Foreign funding up despite tightening of FCRA rules
description: Despite the tightening of regulations, foreign contributions to NGOs have surged. Recently, however, there has been a notable decline in the number of registered NGOs, now totaling merely 14,500 compared to several lakh in the past. The government emphasizes that the amendments focus on specific foreign-funded channels, aiming to enhance oversight without hindering the broader civil society framework.

title: Opposition opposes FCRA bill, says minorities being targeted
description: Rahul Gandhi briefed opposition parties on discussions regarding the delimitation bill.  The opposition maintains its stand on women's reservation within the current Lok Sabha strength.  Discussions also covered the FCRA bill, with concerns raised about its impact on minorities.  Some members noted potential government removal of retrospective effect clauses.  Parliamentary functioning remains contingent on government statements regarding protests and donations.

title: Telangana extends industrial land conversion applications under HILTP till October

title: Amit Shah assured proposed FCRA changes will not be retrospective, says Mizoram CM
description: Chief minister Lalduhoma from Mizoram held a pivotal meeting with Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday, where Shah confirmed that amendments to the FCRA will not have a retroactive effect. Church representatives were also part of the discussion, emphasizing the need for suggestions to safeguard the FCRA. A vital debate on the proposed bill is set for August 12, promising to clarify future legislative actions.

title: SC dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case
description: The Supreme Court has officially closed the chapter on the Bofors payoff case by dismissing an appeal that challenged the Delhi High Court's 2005 ruling, which had previously annulled criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal filed the appeal, but the court decided against allowing more time for arguments, finalizing the legal dispute once and for all.

title: Territorial Army’s contribution significant for govt’s 'Viksit Bharat' vision: Rajnath
description: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh praised the Territorial Army's significant contributions to Viksit Bharat.  The force embodies the citizen-soldier concept, safeguarding borders and maintaining internal security.  Territorial Army personnel provide surge capacity and act as a bridge to society.  They are also first responders during natural calamities and aid environmental conservation efforts.  Ecological task forces have planted ten crore saplings, supporting national climate goals.

title: Gaganyaan makes progress as critical human-rating milestones achieved: Space min
description: India's Gaganyaan mission has achieved significant milestones in developing critical human-rating systems. Propulsion stages and structures for the launch vehicle have been fully developed and tested. Crew safety systems, including the escape system, have also been successfully developed and qualified. The first uncrewed experimental mission is targeted for late 2026. This will be followed by two more uncrewed flights before the maiden human orbital mission.

The Indian government is now reviewing the proposal to ensure it aligns with the integration of indigenous missile systems, with hopes to finalize the agreement by the end of this year.

Aule Space has successfully validated its crucial technology at an ISRO facility, setting the stage for future demonstrations. With plans for a groundbreaking private satellite docking trial next year, this innovation could save billions by prolonging the functionality of essential assets in orbit.

Nearly 200 deaths linked to weight-loss drugs Ozempic and Mounjaro in the UK
description: UK health authorities have recorded almost 200 fatalities linked to the anti-obesity medications Mounjaro and Wegovy. These drugs have been associated with more than 150,000 adverse effects. Notably, semaglutide, which is marketed as Ozempic and Wegovy, accounts for 59 deaths, while tirzepatide, known as Mounjaro, has resulted in 120 deaths and over 106,000 adverse reactions, and liraglutide, or Saxenda, has 37 deaths with 4,528 adverse effects recorded.

description: Justice Veerappa told The Hindu that he found several violations of guidelines with respect to core zone, buffer zone and periphery zone owing to the allowance of commercial activities and homestays in the prohibited area of the Hampi World Heritage Area.

title: Newly elected PoK legislator is on police bail in UK for child sex offences
description: A former PoK minister faces child sex offense allegations from the 1990s.  He was arrested in the UK and is currently out on police bail.  Ahmed allegedly failed to attend a court date, campaigning instead in Mirpur.  A UK judge allowed him to travel to Pakistan despite his bail status.  Greater Manchester police may seek his extradition if he fails to appear.

title: Iltija booked for ‘assaulting’ cop; PDP says she was manhandled
description: An FIR has been filed by J&K Police against Iltija Mufti, accusing her of assaulting an officer amid protests. Charges against her involve public servant assault and rioting, while her mother, Mehbooba Mufti, is also named for failing to adhere to protest regulations. The PDP refutes these claims, asserting police brutality led to Iltija's injuries and criticizing the questioning of an individual in medical care.

title: Landmine blast injures 2 Army personnel in Poonch; rusty shells destroyed in Mankote
description: In the Mendhar sector, two personnel from the Army Bomb Disposal Squad sustained injuries while trying to defuse a dangerous landmine. A nearby team later located and safely destroyed rusty mortar shells in the Mankote sector. The initial discovery of the landmine was made by an Army patrol, which promptly notified the bomb disposal unit.

title: India’s first high-altitude wildlife safari to come up in Ladakh
description: Ladakh administration approved India's first high-altitude wildlife safari to prevent illegal off-roading. This initiative aims to protect snow leopards and bird-watching trails in the region. Guided jeep safaris will be introduced on popular tourist routes across the Union Territory. Local youths will be trained as guides for spotting wildlife and birds. The program promotes community-led conservation and responsible eco-tourism.

title: Wangchuk gives govt 1 month to drop cases, compensate for Leh protest firing
description: In a bold move, the Leh Apex Body has presented the Union government with a one-month ultimatum, calling for the withdrawal of allegations against protesters and support for the families affected by last year’s tragedies. The relatives of four deceased demonstrators are adamant about receiving justice and compensation. They have signaled potential protests if their requests are ignored, underscoring the urgent need for the Centre's attention to Ladakh's pressing concerns.

title: J&K CM visits flood-hit Rajouri, reviews relief measures
description: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah visited flood-affected Rajouri district. He directed authorities to expedite restoration and intensify relief and rehabilitation efforts. The government will enhance relief quantum and provide rehabilitation assistance to affected families. Families losing homes and land will receive five marlas for rehabilitation. Construction along vulnerable riverbanks will not be permitted by the administration.

What began as a casual friendship soon grew stronger, eventually leading Safira to invite Reddy to her childhood village in Germany.

However, it looks like the viral image is fake and was created using artificial intelligence, with the original photograph dating back to 2023.

Rahane snubs MS Dhoni, Virat Kohli; names India's greatest-ever cricketer
description: Ajinkya Rahane recently retired from all cricket formats. He named Sachin Tendulkar as India's greatest-ever cricketer. Tendulkar had a remarkable 24-year international career for India. Rahane played alongside Tendulkar in domestic and IPL matches. He also captained India in all three formats.

title: Australia removed island rabbits in 1986; native habitat is returning
description: Phillip Island has undergone a remarkable environmental turnaround following an extensive pest eradication initiative. The island is witnessing a resurgence of native flora and is nurturing thriving colonies of migratory seabirds. Each year, it becomes a safe haven for thousands of seabirds to breed. Ongoing restoration efforts aim to safeguard native wildlife and reinforce vulnerable soil ecosystems, making it a crucial sanctuary for reptiles that have vanished from other regions.

title: Quote of the day by Larry Page: “You need to get one thing done well, or else…”
description: Larry Page advocates for completing one task well before starting others. This focused approach builds confidence and a strong foundation for future endeavors.  Many fields, including education and business, benefit from this principle of deep mastery.  Rushing tasks can create future problems, while high standards require patience and revision.  This principle remains relevant amidst modern distractions and constant communication shifts.

title: Kentucky family rejects $26M offer for farm land over ‘poison’ data center
description: A Kentucky family has taken a stand against a tempting $26 million proposal for their farmland, which an undisclosed company intended for a grand AI data center. The family champions the importance of preserving agricultural land and food security, emphasizing that their attachment to the property goes beyond mere monetary value. In contrast, other local landowners appear to be more receptive to selling.

title: 'Kya Bolti Public': CJP announces nationwide 'pressure campaign' from September
description: The Cockroach Janata Party is stepping in as a public pressure group, primarily targeting pressing issues such as unemployment and education reform across the country. Set to launch their 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign in September, they aim to engage the youth in dialogue for transparency and accountability. Moreover, the CJP is determined to tackle escalating education costs and improve the reliability of media.

title: After 'ban' on Claude Code, Microsoft has more 'bad news' for Anthropic
description: Microsoft has told engineers that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for" in a new internal memo from EVP Jay Parikh. The memo makes OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default internal model, replacing an auto-router that had been sending GitHub Copilot workloads to Anthropic's Claude. Every Microsoft division now carries an AI token budget target, months after Claude Code licences were cancelled.

title: Family seeks probe after NYPD officer dies following surgery abroad
Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
description: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.
